classification.difficultyReason: Compare the fractional areas of two blue sectors with different denominators and rebut the count-only claim.

inlines.text: Jackson says, “The chance of spinning blue on each spinner is the same because there is one blue section on each spinner.” Explain why Jackson is incorrect.

spec.description: Four equal quadrants; clockwise from the upward radius: R, G, B, Y. No pointer.
spec.mathematics: One blue quadrant out of four equally likely quadrants.
spec.answerVisibility: Outcome labels and sectors are permanent givens; no probability answer is shown.

spec.description: Eight equal sectors; clockwise from the upward radius: R, G, R, Y, B, Y, R, G. Same diameter as spinner A; no pointer.
spec.mathematics: Three red, two green, two yellow and one blue sector; each sector spans 45 degrees.
spec.answerVisibility: Outcome labels and sectors are permanent givens; no probability answer is shown.

answer.short: The blue sections occupy different fractions of the spinners. For spinner A, $P(\text{blue})=\frac14$; for spinner B, $P(\text{blue})=\frac18$.
answer.worked:
The blue sections occupy different fractions of the spinners.
$$\begin{align*}P_A(\text{blue})&=\frac{1}{4}\\P_B(\text{blue})&=\frac{1}{8}\end{align*}$$
Each spinner has one blue section, but A has four equal sections and B has eight. Blue is twice as likely on spinner A.
